conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Leg labels form a finite, possibly empty set; E_i>0, |v_i|<1, Q_i is real, η_i=-1 for incoming and +1 for outgoing legs, and Ση_iQ_i=0. Algebraic contractions use signature (+,-,-,-).

Use SI units: ν=c|k| is angular frequency in s⁻¹, k is in m⁻¹, photon energy is ℏν in joules, and b and C=∫|b|²dΩ are dimensionless. The acceptance A⊆S² is Borel; dΩ is Euclidean chart surface measure.

The transverse one-particle space is the closed subspace of L²(R³;C³) satisfying k·u(k)=0 almost everywhere. Its Hermitian pairing is second-variable-linear; the transverse dot-product condition uses the complex-bilinear extension.

Symmetric sector m uses the averaging projection P_s,m=(1/m!)ΣU_π; sector zero is C. The exponential vector has sector f⊗m/√m!, and its normalized coherent vector is exp(-‖f‖²/2)ε(f). Occupation probabilities are squared projection norms.
Cutoffs satisfy 0<ε<Δ<Λ. The unresolved band is (ε,Δ), and the resolved band is [Δ,Λ); singleton frequencies have zero measure, so endpoint assignments do not affect probabilities.
The Poisson formulas include C=0 using 0!=1 and 0⁰=1. Number divergence and displacement nonconvergence require C>0; at C=0 the displacement is zero at every cutoff.
All probabilities and expectations concern the specified free coherent-state model. They assert no empirical detector response, interacting-QED scattering law, or real–virtual cancellation.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the finite balanced subluminal current, Borel angular acceptance, transverse coherent displacement f_ε,Λ(k)=1_{ε<c|k|<Λ}|k|^(-3/2)b(k/|k|), normalized coherent vector, and band-occupation probabilities.

For every finite partition of (ε,Λ) into disjoint Borel frequency intervals B_j, the coherent state has independent Poisson band counts with means λ_j=C∫_{B_j}dν/ν. For C=0 every band count is zero. The marked one-particle intensity is |b(n)|²dΩ(n)dν/ν.
For 0<ε<Δ<Λ in the defined model, P(N_u=n,N_r=0)=exp(-C log(Λ/ε))(C log(Δ/ε))ⁿ/n! for every n∈N₀. Summing over n gives P(N_r=0)=exp(-C log(Λ/Δ)), independently of ε.

The unresolved coherent vector belongs to D(H_γ), has mean count C log(Δ/ε), and has energy expectation ℏC(Δ-ε). For C>0 the mean count diverges and the displacement has no one-particle norm limit as ε↓0, while energy tends to ℏCΔ. For C=0 the displacement is zero at every cutoff.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact foundational assumption used by the Hilbert, Fock, measure, and second-quantization suppliers.
SI constants, dimensionless coupling g, algebraic metric, and energy-vector conventions; the batch explicitly selects its second-variable-linear pairing.
Hilbert tensor completions, symmetric averaging projections, square-summable Fock sectors, vacuum, and pairing conventions.
Closed positive transverse L² space and its measurable orthogonal projection.
Maximal one-particle multiplier |k| on the transverse space and SI energy multiplier ℏc|k|.

Bounded balanced subluminal current, finite full-sphere angular coefficient, and agreement of energy-coordinate and length-coordinate profiles. The batch uses its angular construction without importing an interacting or empirical claim.
Euclidean contraction, norm, and transverse projection formulas.
Chart definition of dΩ on S² using the Gram Jacobian and subordinate partition.
Identification of Euclidean chart surface measure with the finite polar sphere measure under Countable Choice.
Polar integration of the nonnegative Borel norm and energy integrands, producing radial dν/ν and dν factors.
Radial logarithmic integrals, cutoff splitting, divergence, and strict positivity of the threshold comparison integral.
Power-series definition used for coherent normalization and Poisson sums.
Absolute convergence of exponential series and the shifted moment sums.
Exponential multiplication, normalization cancellation, and agreement with the real exponential.
Factorial recursion, nonzero factorial denominators, and 0!=1.
Natural powers including 0⁰=1 and positive powers of zero.

Sector multiplication by Σ|k_j| with maximal square-integrability domain. The energy proof explicitly identifies vector-valued L² with scalar L² on momentum times a three-point counting space and restricts to the transverse reducing subspace.
Energy proof step 1.2 applies its no-strong-Fock-limit conclusion with κ=Δ/c, δ=ε/c, transverse b∈L², and C_b=C>0. The proposition separately proves its stated one-particle displacement nonlimit.
